children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares ended slightly lower on Thursday, as chip stocks held their ground even as investors awaited key U.S. inflation data due later this week and assessed the inflationary impact of the widening Middle East conflict.
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed down 16.77 points, or 0.24%, at 7,034.93, after falling as much as 2.2%.
** The index briefly turned higher during the session, as chipmakers cut losses.

** "The semiconductor sector held up amid complex macroeconomic conditions. The focus is on U.S. inflation data and the Federal Reserve's policy meeting (next week)," said Kim Joon-young, analyst at iM Securities.
** Brent crude breached $100 a barrel after Iran and U.S. struck tankers in the biggest wave of attacks on shipping since the war began in February.

** A Bank of Korea board member said the central bank would assess external and internal policy conditions, including the impact of the previous two rate hikes, to determine the timing and pace of further tightening.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
fell 0.19%, while peer SK Hynix
lost 0.16%.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 1.62%, while Hyundai Motor
and automaker Kia Corp
were up 0.26% and 0.16%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
added 0.59%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
fell 2%.
** Of the total 915 traded issues, 421 shares advanced, while 440 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 962.0 billion won ($718.78 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,339.2 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.07% higher than its previous close at 1,340.2.
** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.08 point to 102.96.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 2.4 basis points to 3.930%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
rose by 6.2 basis points to 4.452%.
